correctness.rationale: Proof checks: F P_d integer polynomial; for odd d, alternating squared binomial sum gives root at -d-1 and Q_d integer; P_d(c)>c+d+1; modulo q critical value and integer divisibility imply either m|d! or q|K_d. K_d calculated by two independent exact formulas. Each of all 639114 m|d! candidates checked by exact nth roots; every odd prime factor of K_d is exhausted using monotone equation search with complete remainder=1 factor check. No c or q bound is assumed. Both branches empty for d=9,11,...,25. Included script and captured output suffice to rerun the finite certificate.

value.rationale: The source poses nonexistence for all odd d as an explicit open question. Previously d=3,5 were resolved and a separate published d=7 result is indexed. Nine consecutive next odd exponent layers are resolved with an algebraic factorial-divisor sieve and exact full-fiber arithmetic certification, not a cutoff search. This natural systematic classification and reusable exceptional-prime obstruction have clear structural motivation; it does not claim to settle d>=27.
